articles.title: Champions League 2026-27 draw: Four pots set as 36 clubs discover their league-phase opponents in star-studded fixtures
articles.summary: Football News: The Champions League 2026-27 draw features thrilling matchups including Arsenal vs Real Madrid and Manchester United vs Bayern Munich. Discover the full list of fixtures and the teams involved in this star-studded league phase.
articles.body: The Champions League has its 36-team field, its four seeding pots and, following Thursday's draw in Monaco, a complete set of league-phase opponents. This season's draw has produced several heavyweight meetings, including Arsenal hosting Real Madrid and travelling to Bayern Munich, Liverpool welcoming Atlético Madrid before heading to Inter Milan, and Manchester City being paired with defending champions Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona.Manchester United's return to Europe's elite also brings a blockbuster reunion with Bayern Munich at Old Trafford, while Aston Villa have been handed a particularly glamorous reward for winning the Europa League. With every team facing eight different opponents, here is how the new Champions League campaign has been put together.How the Champions League league phase worksThe 36 clubs are divided into four pots according to their UEFA coefficient rankings and results in European competition over the previous five years.Each club is then drawn against two teams from each pot, giving every side eight league-phase matches in total.The schedule is split evenly between home and away fixtures, so every club will play four matches at home and four away. Across the entire league phase, that produces 144 matches.The format also determines what happens after those eight games. The top eight teams in the standings advance directly to the round of 16, while teams finishing from ninth through 24th enter the knockout-phase play-offs. The remaining sides are eliminated.There are also important restrictions on the draw. The five Premier League clubs cannot be drawn against one another during the league phase, while UEFA has introduced a further condition preventing the same fixture from being repeated with the same home team for three consecutive seasons.That means Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid again, while Inter Milan cannot host Arsenal again, after those fixtures were played with the same home teams in the previous two seasons.Pot 1: The European heavyweightsThe first pot contains the defending champions and some of the biggest names in European football, giving the teams drawn from the lower pots the possibility of facing some formidable opposition.Paris Saint-GermainBayern MunichReal MadridLiverpoolInter MilanManchester CityArsenalBarcelonaAtlético MadridParis Saint-Germain enter as the two-time defending European champions, having beaten Arsenal in last season's final.Pot 2: United return alongside European heavyweightsManchester United are back in the Champions League after a two-year absence and will be drawn from the second pot.Borussia DortmundRomaSporting CPAston VillaPortoManchester UnitedClub BruggeReal BetisPSV EindhovenAston Villa also enter this group after winning the Europa League, while Dortmund and Porto bring their own European pedigree.Pot 3: A dangerous middle groundPot 3 contains several clubs capable of making life difficult for the competition's traditional giants.FeyenoordLilleBodø/GlimtNapoliRB LeipzigVillarrealFenerbahçeShakhtar DonetskGalatasarayBodø/Glimt will be particularly familiar to viewers who followed last season's competition. articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo reportedly 'crying intensely' after Al-Nassr comeback as journalist reveals why he came off at half-time
articles.summary: Football News: Cristiano Ronaldo reportedly cried after Al-Nassr's thrilling 3-2 win over Al-Ettifaq, claiming he wasn't fit to continue. Despite being substituted at half-time, Ronaldo passionately cheered on his teammates from the sidelines.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo reportedly endured an emotional night despite Al-Nassr completing one of the most remarkable comebacks of their season, with Saudi Arabian media personality Khalid Al-Shanif claiming the Portugal star was "crying intensely" after the 3-2 victory over Al-Ettifaq.The 41-year-old made his first start of the season on Tuesday, but was replaced by Abdullah Al-Khaibari at half-time after Al-Nassr had fallen 2-0 behind and been reduced to 10 men. Al-Shanif has since offered his account of what happened behind the scenes, while manager Ange Postecoglou gave a somewhat different explanation of the substitution, saying Ronaldo was always scheduled to play only the opening 45 minutes.What happened with Ronaldo at half-time?Al-Nassr's night had started badly when goalkeeper Bento was sent off in the 12th minute after bringing down Moussa Dembélé, forcing the team to play almost the entire match with 10 men.Al-Ettifaq then took advantage of the numerical advantage, with Ondrej Duda putting the hosts ahead in the 31st minute before Álvaro Medrán doubled the lead in first-half stoppage time.Ronaldo, who had only recently returned to competitive action after an extended break following the 2026 World Cup and his marriage to Georgina Rodríguez, was subsequently replaced at the interval, with Al-Khaibari coming on as Al-Nassr looked to strengthen the team after going down to 10 men.According to Saudi Arabian sports journalist and television presenter Al-Shanif, who discussed the situation on his programme Doreena Ghair, the decision was actually initiated by Ronaldo himself."Cristiano Ronaldo was the one who requested to be substituted against Al-Ettifaq because he wasn't ready and wanted a ready player in his place. Cristiano Ronaldo was crying intensely after Al-Nassr's victory against Al-Ettifaq."Reports and footage from the match also fuelled speculation that Ronaldo was angry with the decision. The Al-Nassr captain was visibly irritated as he removed the armband from his arm and walked off the pitch.Postecoglou says Ronaldo was always meant to play 45 minutesSpeaking after the match, Postecoglou explained that Ronaldo's limited involvement was linked to his fitness rather than a reaction to his performance."Look, again, with Cristiano, he is a unique sportsman. He has not had much preparation, and the plan was always for him to play 45 minutes against Al Ettifaq. He played 30 minutes in the first game, so we wanted him to play 45 against Al Ettifaq and build up gradually."The manager added that Ronaldo had wanted to remain on the pitch after Al-Nassr fell two goals behind."That was always going to happen at half time, but because of the situation, with the team losing 2-0, Cristiano wanted to help and wanted to keep playing. For me, though, those 45 minutes were good because now we know that he is ready to play more than 45 minutes. I know he feels physically in good condition now, so he is ready for tomorrow's game."Ronaldo cheers Al-Nassr's comeback from the sidelinesWhatever the circumstances surrounding the substitution, Ronaldo watched from the sidelines as his team produced a stunning turnaround — and footage from the second half showed him loudly and proudly cheering his teammates on.Al-Nassr came out for the second half two goals down and a man short, but they gradually turned the game around. Sadio Mané pulled one back in the 74th minute after João Félix threaded a pass through to him, giving the visitors a route back into the match.Only three minutes later, Félix provided the delivery again, this time from a corner, and Abdulelah Al-Amri headed Al-Nassr level.With the match seemingly heading towards a draw, Al-Nassr found one final opening in the 90th minute. Sami Al-Najei drove the counter-attack forward before finding Mané, who finished from inside the box to complete his brace and send Al-Nassr from 2-0 down to a 3-2 victory.The celebrations continued inside the dressing room, where visuals showed Ronaldo embracing his teammates after the dramatic turnaround. Despite being unable to influence the result on the pitch, he appeared fully invested in the victory, sharing the emotional scenes with the squad after the final whistle.The result leaves Al-Nassr with a perfect nine points from their opening three Saudi Pro League matches.Ronaldo's return is still being managedRonaldo missed Al-Nassr's opening two league matches against Al-Fateh and Al-Diriyah while taking an extended break following Portugal's World Cup campaign and his wedding to Rodríguez.He returned as a substitute against Al-Riyadh and scored before making his first start of the season against Al-Ettifaq.Postecoglou's comments suggest Al-Nassr are still carefully managing his workload, although the manager believes Ronaldo is now ready to play beyond the 45-minute mark.Al-Nassr will next face Al-Taawoun as they look to maintain their perfect start to the Saudi Pro League season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chelsea agree to sign Lionel Messi's World Cup winning Argentina teammate in £7.5m deal
articles.summary: Football News: Chelsea have agreed a £7.5 million deal to sign Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez ahead of the summer transfer deadline, BBC reported.The 33-ye.
articles.body: Chelsea have agreed a £7.5 million deal to sign Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez ahead of the summer transfer deadline, BBC reported.The 33-year-old Argentina international is set to undergo a medical in London before joining Chelsea's goalkeeping group at Stamford Bridge.The move comes after concerns over the performances of Robert Sanchez, especially during Chelsea's 3-2 win over Fulham on Monday.Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso had identified signing a goalkeeper as a priority after Sanchez's display against Fulham. The deal for Martinez was completed quickly after that decision.Martinez has fallen out of favour at Aston Villa following the club's signing of Japan goalkeeper Zion Suzuki from Parma earlier this month for around £30 million. Martinez is expected to sign a two-year contract with Chelsea, with an option to extend it by another year.Sanchez has been Chelsea's first-choice goalkeeper since 2023. Against Fulham, he allowed Josh King's shot to slip through his hands at the near post. Later in the match, he spilled another effort into a dangerous area, allowing Gonzalo Garcia to score.Chelsea had previously backed Sanchez as their first-choice goalkeeper, but the club has now decided to bring in Martinez just days before the transfer window closes.Chelsea also have Mike Penders, who joined from Genk for £17 million, as another goalkeeping option. He is expected to make his debut in the Carabao Cup against Luton Town on Thursday night.Chelsea are also expected to have a busy end to the transfer window as Manchester City continue their attempts to sign Enzo Fernandez. The Argentina midfielder wants to leave Chelsea and was left out of the squad for Thursday night's Carabao Cup match against Luton.The transfer is another deal between Chelsea and Aston Villa in recent weeks.Chelsea signed Morgan Rogers from Villa for a club-record £117 million, while Alejandro Garnacho moved to Villa on an initial loan deal last month.Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson was completing a medical at Villa Park on Thursday as he prepares to reunite with his former Villarreal manager Unai Emery. Villa value the deal at around £65 million.The two clubs have completed several transfers recently, including Ian Maatsen joining Villa and Omari Kellyman moving to Chelsea in a deal that was widely described as a PSR swap.Martinez had also attracted interest from Juventus earlier in the transfer window, but that move collapsed because of concerns over a finger injury. articles.title: El sorteo de la Champions dispara al Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: Bet365 sitúa al conjunto blanco como el favorito para acabar líder la fase liga
articles.summary: Bet365 sitúa al conjunto blanco como el favorito para acabar líder la fase liga
articles.body: La suerte ya está echada y los cinco equipos españoles que participan en esta Champions 26-27 ya conocen cuáles serán sus ocho rivales en la fase liga. El sorteo ha dibujado caminos muy diferentes para Barcelona, Real Madrid, Atlético de Madrid, Betis y Villarreal. El gran objetivo será, como siempre, finalizar entre los ocho primeros para obtener el billete directo a octavos de final o, en su defecto, recurrir a la ronda de 'playoffs'. El curso pasado, donde también participaron cinco representantes españoles, sólo el Barcelona consiguió terminar entre los ocho primeros. Real Madrid y Atlético de Madrid tuvieron que pasar por el 'playoff' para alcanzar los octavos, mientras que Villarreal y Athletic Club quedaron eliminados en la primera ronda. Esta temporada, el escenario vuelve a ser exigente... aunque el sorteo ha dejado sensaciones diferentes. Las apuestas deportivas también han reaccionado a los emparejamientos y, especialmente, al camino que tendrá por delante el Real Madrid. En esta ocasión, Bet365 vuelve a situar al Barcelona entre los ocho primeros con una cuota de 1.53. El conjunto azulgrana se enfrentará a Manchester City, PSG, Aston Villa, Sporting CP, Feyenoord, Galatasaray, Como y Sabah. Un calendario que combina varios rivales de máxima exigencia con otros, teóricamente, más asequibles. Sin embargo, el gran beneficiado entre los españoles parece ser el Real Madrid. Bet365 le asigna una cuota de 1.44 para acabar en el Top-8 y, además, le coloca como favorito para terminar líder de la fase liga con una cuota de 5.5. Todo ello, pese a que en las dos ediciones anteriores nunca logró clasificarse directamente entre los ocho primeros. El calendario del Real Madrid estará compuesto por Inter, Arsenal, PSV, Roma, Leipzig, Shakhtar, LASK y AEK. Un camino que permitirá medir si realmente están en esa posición. Mucho menos favorable ha sido el sorteo para el Atlético de Madrid, que tendrá que enfrentarse a Bayern, Liverpool, Manchester United, PSV, Fenerbahçe, Bodo/Glimt, Viking y Stuttgart. Bet365 le sitúa fuera del Top-8 con una cuota de 3.0. Betis y Villarreal, por su parte, ya eran conscientes de que tendrían un camino complicado y el objetivo pasa por alcanzar al menos el 'playoff': la cuota es de 1.73 para los verdiblancos y de 1.67 para el conjunto castellonense. Las mejores casas de apuestas ya empiezan a marcar diferencias claras entre los cinco españoles. Después del sorteo, el PSG continúa siendo el principal favorito para revalidar el título por tercera temporada consecutiva con una cuota de 6.0 en Bet365. Barcelona, Bayern y Arsenal aparecen inmediatamente por detrás, todos ellos con 7.0, mientras que el Real Madrid cierra el Top-5 con una cuota de 7.5. Queda mucho camino por delante hasta la final del Metropolitano, pero los cinco representantes españoles ya conocen su futuro más inmediato. Al menos de momento, el sorteo ha disparado las expectativas en torno al Real Madrid.

articles.title: 2. Bundesliga Preview: Hertha hope to maintain perfect record, Osnabrück seek maiden point
articles.summary: The third matchday of 2. Bundesliga will commence with a couple of fixtures on Friday. Hertha BSC will face Eintracht Braunschweig away from home as they hop...
articles.body:
The third matchday of 2. Bundesliga will commence with a couple of fixtures on Friday. Hertha BSC will face Eintracht Braunschweig away from home as they hope to extend their winning streak, while VfL Bochum host pointless VfL Osnabrück.

Hertha BSC are unbeaten in their last six head-to-head fixtures against Eintracht Braunschweig. Furthermore, the visitors won their first three games of the season, although they needed a penalty shootout to knock out Pokal specialists Saarbrücken.

Eintracht Braunschweig had a dream start to the season with a 6-1 victory over Magdeburg in the opening 2. Bundesliga matchday before home defeats to Bochum and Union Berlin in two competitions.

Deyovaisio Zeefuik is suspended after his red card in Hertha's 4-1 win over Heidenheim, but new signing Mads Pedersen could fill the position. Meanwhile, Marten Winkler, who was involved in three of the goals back then, has since left the club to join Anderlecht.

Braunschweig: Hoffmann; Aydin, Ehlers, Hoti, Katterbach; Flick; Di Benedetto, Marie; Sturm, Entrup, Opoku

Hertha: Gersbeck; Eitschberger, Gechter, Kolbe, Pedersen; Seguin, Sessa; Thorsteinsson, Gouram, Brekalo ©; Grönning

Days before facing FC Bayern in the DFB-Pokal first round tie, Osnabrück will face Bochum away from home in 2. Bundesliga. The newly-promoted side started their campaign with two defeats, although the positives outweigh the 4-3 defeat to Heidenheim on the opening matchday.

Bochum recovered from a home defeat to Hertha in the season's curtain-raiser with victories on the road in 2. Bundesliga and Pokal. Uwe Rösler's men will now have another chance to keep the momentum as they hope to get involved in the promotion race.

Bochum are unbeaten against Osnabrück in eight meetings, with their last head-to-head fixture dating back to the 2020/21 season. However, the Purple-Whites held Bochum to draws in their last two visits to Vonovia Ruhrstadion.

articles.title: Rodri’s debut, Cubarsi’s return | Three takeaways from Barcelona 2-0 Athletic Club
articles.summary: Barcelona made it six points in two games with their win over Athletic Club last night as they took the Basque giants down with a 2-0 scoreline at the Spotif...
articles.body:
Barcelona made it six points in two games with their win over Athletic Club last night as they took the Basque giants down with a 2-0 scoreline at the Spotify Camp Nou.

Pedri, Pau Cubarsi and Anthony Gordon entered the starting lineup on the night and the team looked comfortable, yet threatening from the get-go.

Raphinha eventually scored the opener with some wonderful footwork and Barcelona toiled to earn the second goal to pull free of the competition.

Eventually, a bit of luck and Fermin Lopez's lethality helped the team secure the 2-0 win and helped them back to the top of the table.

Barça Universal brings you three takeaways from Barcelona 2-0 Athletic Club.

Going purely by the scoreline, Barcelona's win over Elche appears significantly more dominant than their win last night over Athletic Club de Bilbao. The reality, however, is very different.

Unai Simon played a fantastic game against Barcelona. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Taking to the field last night for the second official game of the season, Barcelona were dominant from the get-go and relentlessly attacked the visitors, even more than they did against Elche.

The scoreline, however, tells a different story, and that was only down to one man – Unai Simon.

On the night at Spotify Camp Nou, the Spanish national team goalkeeper showed his class and bailed his team out of difficult situations repeatedly. In 90 minutes, he made a staggering eight saves, six of which came from inside the box.

Had it not been for Simon, the scoreline could well have been 6-0 or even 7-0 in Barcelona's favour, for they hit the woodwork twice and were denied by Simon's brilliance time and time again beyond the two goals that counted.

If anything, the performance only solidifies the argument that Barcelona's attack looks lethal without a striker for the second straight game. After all, the team created four big chances and had an xG of 4.23 compared to the opposition's 0.25.

Pau Cubarsi made his first official appearance of the new season last night. It was, in fact, his first start in a competitive game since the FIFA World Cup final.

Pau Cubarsi returned to the starting XI. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Rightfully named the Best Young Player at the World Cup, Cubarsi picked up exactly where he left off and showed no signs of rustiness despite playing after over a month.

The young defender's reading of the game was immaculate, and he placed himself in the best strategic position to nullify the opposition's attacking threat. His defensive contributions were well-timed, and his distribution was silky as always.

In 90 minutes, the teenage sensation made two tackles, three clearances and won five duels. He completed 95% of his passes and was crucial to the clean sheet being maintained.

Barcelona's defence looked superior in terms of the cohesion and implementation of the high line with the youngster back, and it is clear at this point that he is another young anomaly of the sport.

His return to club football in top condition, needless to say, comes as a massive boost to Hansi Flick's plans.

The one moment Barcelona's game last night will be remembered for in the years to come was the 63rd minute of the game when the club's latest and marquee signing Rodri took to the field to make his official debut.

Rodri made his official debut for Barcelona. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Having only completed his transfer last week, it was unclear when fans would get to see him in action for the first time. After all, he also underwent recent surgery on his back.

Despite everything, however, the player began training with the group in no time and came off the bench for his official debut against Athletic Club. He played the final half an hour, and his integration seemed effortless.

Playing in a system constructed to maximise his strengths, Rodri looked comfortable playing as Barcelona's pivot and linked up well with Pedri, Dani Olmo, Cubarsi and Fermin Lopez.

The team instantly shifted to a traditional 4-3-3 after his arrival, making it clear what role Flick sees best suited for Rodri. Pedri moved into an attacking midfield role, and the new signing held the fortress with ease.

There is no doubt that the player is still rusty and will take some time to adapt and enhance his link-up with the existing players. What last night's game showed, however, is that it will not take too long.

In just 27 minutes, the former Manchester City star made 23 accurate passes with an accuracy rate of 88%. He also made one key pass and had three defensive contributions with three ground duels won at a 100% success rate.

It remains to be seen when the player is fit enough to start, but it is safe to say that Rodri's debut was promising and that the team will move several notches up in terms of stability with him holding the fortress.

articles.summary: Yan Diomande arrived at Real Madrid this summer with a record-breaking price tag and the expectations that come with it. Two games into the 2026/27 La Liga s...
articles.body:
Yan Diomande arrived at Real Madrid this summer with a record-breaking price tag and the expectations that come with it.

Two games into the 2026/27 La Liga season, though, the €125 million signing is still waiting for his first real moment in the spotlight.

Real Madrid have started strongly, and the usual names have taken over the headlines.

As such, Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Jr. and Jude Bellingham have driven the early conversation around the club, while Mourinho's new-look side has shown enough attacking fluency to give the manager little reason to force changes.

That has left Diomande in an unfamiliar position, with Real Madrid's most expensive signing playing just over 30 minutes across the opening two league matches.

For a 19-year-old signed from Leipzig, the lack of immediate prominence should not necessarily be mistaken for a lack of belief.

But given the price tag attached to his name, questions are being raised.

Guler's emergence has complicated the picture

Arda Guler is Diomande's immediate competition. (Photo by David Balogh/Getty Images)

Diomande's biggest obstacle is not just the competition created by Vinicius or the presence of Mbappe and Bellingham.

Arda Guler's new role under Jose Mourinho has also changed the balance of Real Madrid's attack.

Mourinho has used a 4-2-3-1 in the first two competitive matches, with Guler beginning from the right before moving into central areas when Madrid have the ball.

The tactical adjustment has given the Turkish international a more prominent role and, in turn, reduced the immediate need for another natural winger.

Diomande was introduced against Espanyol when the score stood at 1-1, offering Mourinho an attacking option during a competitive second half.

His appearance against Real Sociedad was shorter still. With Madrid already in control, the Ivorian replaced Vinicius in the 84th minute.

Those cameos have offered only glimpses of what the Real Madrid hierarchy paid so heavily to acquire.

A record transfer fee does not buy a place

Yan Diomande is Real Madrid's club-record signing. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

The Yan Diomande transfer was one of the defining moves of Real Madrid's summer.

At €125 million, with the potential of rising to €140 million, the club made a statement about how highly they rate the teenager.

Yet Mourinho has shown no sign of selecting players according to their transfer fee.

With Real Madrid winning and their attacking structure functioning, the Portuguese coach has understandably placed trust in the players who have started the season well.

Vinicius remains a decisive presence, while Guler's ability to operate from the right and drift into midfield has given Mourinho another tactical solution.

That is the reality Diomande must understand. He is not arriving at a struggling side crying out for reinvention.

Rather, he is trying to break into one of the deepest and most talented attacks in European football.

Indeed, the coming weeks should offer more opportunities, as the fixture list will become heavier and rotation will be required, but that still does not guarantee anything.

Diomande has not played much for Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

There is a temptation to judge a €125 million signing, particularly when the player has been limited to a handful of minutes.

But Diomande's first weeks at Real Madrid may say more about the competition around him than his standing within the club.

At 19, he has time on his side. What he needs now is the right opportunity.

Mourinho's selection against Espanyol and Real Sociedad suggests that Diomande is still being introduced gradually, rather than being handed responsibility because of the size of his transfer.

That approach could frustrate fans expecting an immediate impact, but it also shows the reality of Real Madrid's current attacking strength.

The first opening may come through rotation. When it does, the focus will shift from the size of the Yan Diomande transfer fee to a more important question: can Real Madrid's record signing make himself impossible to leave out?

articles.title: EFL five things: Early days but the pressure is on
articles.summary: BBC Sport picks out five highlights to keep an eye on in Saturday's busy EFL programme.
articles.body:
We may only be three weeks into the new EFL season but you can sense there is already a little twitchiness among some fanbases.

Not winning either of your first couple of league games brings unwanted attention - just ask West Ham, Stoke, Norwich and Burnley.

In League One, Plymouth Argyle's slow start last season ultimately cost them at least a play-off spot and it has been another sluggish opening as they prepare to host a buoyant Bradford City.

Salford City and Gillingham have been big spenders in recent seasons in League Two and yet remain mired in the fourth tier with their respective starts hardly giving cause for optimism - here are five things we have picked out to keep an eye on in the EFL this Saturday.

Relegation from the Premier League is only temporary, right? I mean, teams who come down go straight back up don't they?

Try telling that to Stoke City fans who are watching their team play Championship football for the ninth successive season, with a highest finish of 14th since dropping out of the top flight.

That did seem to be changing last season when, just over a third of the way through the campaign, they were second with a play-off place at the very least seeming inevitable.

But three wins from their final 20 games put those hopes to bed and this season has started with defeats by Swansea and Southampton.

But it is not for the want of trying by the Potters' owners, who continue to stump up the cash for signings to try to get them out of the Championship, with Ipswich's George Hirst arriving on a permanent deal and team-mate Ben Johnson coming in on a season-loan within the past fortnight.

Mark Robins is the seventh manager to attempt to get Stoke motoring again but that finish to last season and the start to this one has left some restless in their seats - a visit to Wolves on Saturday (12:30 BST) may not help things either.

If you were searching for optimism at the start of the season then you could have looked no further than Norwich City.

Relegation fodder when Philippe Clement took over in November, they eventually finished ninth, winning 17 of 31 league games that the Belgian took charge of.

A summer of careful transfer business including the likes of winger Andre Brooks from Sheffield United after already adding the impressive Ali Ahmed and Mohamed Toure in the new year window pointed towards a promotion challenge.

We may only be two games in but a home defeat by West Brom and a horror display at Millwall leaves them with no points and some head scratching to do.

Relegated Burnley head to Norfolk on Saturday (15:00 BST) and the Clarets are hardly enjoying their return to the Championship under new boss Nicky Hayen, with last weekend's loss at West Brom followed by a midweek EFL Cup exit at Bradford City.

There is still plenty of time for these two to get it right but time is a commodity not often afforded Championship managers.

Yes, we are talking about West Ham United again - they are difficult not to talk about at the moment.

Ownership wrangles and on-field failures make the perfect cocktail for endless headlines and stories.

Breaking the Championship transfer record to sign forward Arne Engels, and then for boss Nuno Espirito Santo to say it is with a view to him playing in the Premier League only draws more attention and pressure.

Losing at home to Charlton last weekend increased that pressure to a level that an EFL Cup win at Southampton on Tuesday will have done little to dampen.

Suddenly a short trip to Watford on Saturday (15:00 BST) looks to be littered with potential pitfalls, more so given the Hornets were themselves impressive winners over Southampton on the opening weekend before earning a notable draw at Wrexham.

Alessio Dionisi's much-changed side may have been thrashed at home by Peterborough in the EFL Cup in midweek but they seem to already have the taste for ruffling the feathers of those more fancied sides. West Ham beware.

Less patient owners may already have Tom Cleverley in the 'former Plymouth manager' bracket but those in south Devon are willing to take a longer-term view it would seem and that stance almost paid off last season.

Fourth from bottom in League One at the turn of the year, Argyle went into the final day of last season still in with a shot at the play-offs before having to settle for eighth place.

So, much like Norwich in the Championship, the start of this season was filled with optimism - but an opening day home defeat by Stockport and a point at Wycombe has reminded fans League One is a tough nut to crack.

It will not get any easier on Saturday (15:00 BST) when Bradford City come calling.

Fresh from reaching the play-offs last season after promotion from League Two, the Bantams have opened their campaign with wins over Peterborough and Sheffield Wednesday plus an EFL Cup upset victory against Burnley - all without conceding a goal.

The bigger they are, the harder they fall - a saying Salford City and Gillingham fans would do well to heed.

Two of League Two's bigger spenders in recent seasons, they are already finding the target on their backs a heavy one to carry.

The Ammies have paid undisclosed fees to tempt both Luke Molyneux (Doncaster) and Brendan Wiredu (Plymouth) to drop down from League One and try to finally help get them out of the fourth tier where they have been since promotion in 2019.

New boss Peter Cklamovski left his role as Malaysia's head coach to join Salford in June and defeats by Barnet and Chesterfield mean a win against pointless Shrewsbury on Saturday (15:00 BST) would steady the nerves a little.

A dozen new summer signings to go with splashing the cash on striker Ronan Hale in January has given Gillingham boss Gareth Ainsworth what he is calling 'his team' and 'his era.' Now they just need to start winning.

The past two seasons have seen the Gills start strongly but subside to successive 17th-place finishes.

Maybe this year will be different given they have taken only one point from two games and were trounced 3-0 at home by Walsall on a sobering first day.

Relegated Northampton head to Priestfield on Saturday (15:00 BST) in a similar situation under new head coach Chris Hogg.

BBC Sport will have live text coverage of all the weekend's EFL action starting with Wrexham v Birmingham City on Friday (20:00 BST).

articles.title: Hugo Duro y el mercado: por ocho no, por 15 sí
articles.standfirst: Clubes han hecho consultas con cifras de por medio, sin llevar a efecto la oferta por escrito porque el Valencia le ha puesto un precio y está dispuesto siempre que se llegue a lo que pide
articles.summary: Clubes han hecho consultas con cifras de por medio, sin llevar a efecto la oferta por escrito porque el Valencia le ha puesto un precio y está dispuesto siempre que se llegue a lo que pide
articles.body: El Valencia ha recibido este verano consultas por algunos jugadores -pocos- y uno por los que se han interesado es Hugo Duro. Desde la entidad se ha abanderado este verano que no hay necesidad de vender jugadores -pese a los grilletes que tienen para poder cerrar fichajes motivo por el que se están viendo mermados- y que se remiten a las cláusulas, pero no es del todo así. Porque el mercado es lo que es. Esa ley de la oferta y la demanda está siempre activa y cabe recordar que si por algo se ha caracterizado este Valencia es porque lo vende todo. Y ha habido consultas de clubes, a través de intermediarios, por ver si el Valencia aceptaba negociar por Duro. En las mismas se ha hablado de ofertas que rondaban los ocho millones de euros. No formal. No por escrito. Pero sí consulta con cifras. Un tanteo. Y el Valencia ha respondido que no aceptaba con lo que no se han trasladado ofertas de manera formal. O sea, a través de una propuesta por escrito. El Valencia está abierto a sentarse. Y le ha puesto una cifra de traspaso al atacante madrileño. Por 15 millones de euros sí admiten la operación (porque ha hecho una media de más de 10 goles los últimos años). Y el motivo es que si se vende hay que buscar otro delantero de garantías y por ocho o nueve millones no lo hay en el mercado... pero por 15 sí pueden darse soluciones. El caso de Hugo Duro es llamativo. Porque es el goleador de este equipo los últimos años... contra viento y marea. Y eso que no ha sido del gusto de los entrenadores. Vuelve a ocurrir lo mismo con Corberán en cuyos pensamientos ha estado que Sadiq esté por delante del getafense... e incluso podría pasar lo mismo con Danjuma si sigue ofreciendo las prestaciones que ha empezado a destapar esta pretemporada actuando de '9'. En resumidas cuentas, que a nivel deportivo no importaría que Duro saliera de la plantilla. Pese a las prestaciones ofensivas que ha mostrado -es el máximo artillero temporada tras temporada- siempre hay cierto halo de dudas con el atacante. No ha sido indiscutible con Corberán. Se ha pasado muchos partidos en el banquillo. No encaja en la filosofía que pretende.... pero los goles que ha hecho le han 'salvado'. Se trata de una de las historias más curiosas de los últimos años en Mestalla.

articles.title: Oficial: Sarr llega cedido desde el Chelsea
articles.standfirst: El jovencísimo central internacional con Senegal que no contaba para Xabi Alonso se convierte en la primera incorporación de la Real para la temporada 2026-27
articles.summary: El jovencísimo central internacional con Senegal que no contaba para Xabi Alonso se convierte en la primera incorporación de la Real para la temporada 2026-27
articles.body: La Real Sociedad ha hecho oficial la incorporación de Mamadou Sarr como cedido desde el Chelsea de Xabi Alonso para la temporada 2026-27, convirtiéndose el jovencísimo central internacional por Senegal, que mañana cumple 21 años, en la primera incorporación para el equipo de Pellegrino Matarazzo de cara a una temporada 2026-27 que ya ha arrancado. Todo apunta a que esta mañana entrenará ya con sus nuevos compañeros y habrá que ver si entra en la convocatoria para el encuentro de mañana en Anoeta frente al Espanyol, aunque parezca demasiado pronto. Sarr, que mide 1,94 metros, es el elegido para reforzar la defensa de una Real que no pudo cerrar antes otras adquisiciones y tuvo que recurrir a este joven central que no entraba en los planes de Xabi Alonso, que ha sido importante en la operación. El internacional con Senegal apunta a formar con Jon Martín, que tiene 20 años, la pareja de centrales más joven de LaLiga y probablemente de todos los campeonatos de Primera división. Es un jugador de un enorme potencial, pero desde febrero apenas ha jugado 150 minutos repartidos en cuatro partidos, por lo que la incógnita es el estado físico en el que llega y si estará ya para ser de la partida en alguno de los cuatro partidos que el equipo guipuzcoano va a tener en los próximos 16 días.

articles.title: El año I de la Liga F con Gasol16 Ventures: tras 156 millones de apuesta público-privada
articles.standfirst: Desde su fundación en 2022, la competición ha recibido un mínimo de 33 millones del Gobierno, que le acaba de incluir en La Quiniela
articles.summary: Desde su fundación en 2022, la competición ha recibido un mínimo de 33 millones del Gobierno, que le acaba de incluir en La Quiniela
articles.body: El reestreno en La Quiniela es una de las grandes novedades que trae la Liga F esta temporada fuera del césped. Su vuelta al tradicional juego de predicciones controlado por el Gobierno –ahora ya con plaza fija– es el último empujón que ha recibido la liga profesional de fútbol femenino para su despegue en visibilidad y, por supuesto, en negocio. Desde su fundación en 2022, la competición y sus clubes han recibido 93 millones de euros de sus socios públicos y privados. La cifra se disparará hasta los 156 millones esta temporada, en buena parte, por los 55 millones ya garantizados por Gasol16 Ventures, el vehículo inversor de Pau Gasol, y Fortified Partners. El exjugador de baloncesto apoyará a la liga en su objetivo de crear un ecosistema propio autosostenible, desligado del fútbol masculino, tras una temporada en la que las audiencias alcanzaron los 7,5 millones de espectadores. Pero también en pleno debate sobre cuál es realmente el techo de la competición como producto de entretenimiento, tras algo más de cinco años en los que el pulmón financiero del Estado y el ecosistema de LaLiga han sido el motor de su negocio. Éste ha sido el camino y los socios que le han acompañado en el camino: Si hoy se puede afirmar que hay una liga profesional de fútbol femenino es porque el Gobierno ha tenido una influencia capital. Primero, por la defensa férrea que hizo de la nueva competición tras la pandemia para darle este estatus, y segundo, un aspecto tan importante o más que el jurídico, por la aportación inicial comprometida para impulsar su profesionalización. De entrada, el CSD puso 33 millones de euros encima de la mesa en 2022, entre los 18 millones para los clubes –principalmente, para instalaciones– y los 15 millones para la propia Liga F. Esta segunda partida, dividida en 5 millones anuales entre 2022 y 2025, tenía el objetivo de que la gestora tuviera recursos y capital para arrancar con su estructura y el desarrollo de su plan de negocio. Estas subvenciones no han sido siempre aprovechadas –el Alhama no se benefició de un millón de euros al no presentar el convenio requerido para la construcción de un campo nuevo– y han generado molestias en otras ligas profesionales, también de reciente creación y que no han tenido el mismo apoyo público. Acabado este ciclo inversor mediante ayudas finalistas, el Gobierno mantendrá la aportación de 5 millones de euros por temporada a través de la ya mentada quiniela. Confeccionada la estructura directiva, liderada por Beatriz Álvarez Mesa, que seguirá en la presidencia hasta 2030 tras su reciente renovación, la Liga Profesional de Fútbol Femenino (LPFF) encontró un hermano mayor en LaLiga. El fútbol masculino, cuyos clubes ya eran mayoría entre los representantes de la categoría –hoy lo son más–, apostó por la competición convirtiéndose en agencia comercial en exclusiva. Es decir, LaLiga le buscaba los patrocinadores en sus activos principales en venta. A cambio, le garantizaba 42 millones de euros en cinco temporadas con un contrato creciente. En este tiempo se ha generado una cartera de socios compuesta por Puma (balón oficial), Volkswagen, EA Sports, Mahou, Solán de Cabras y Panini. Aunque su principal socio actual es Moeve, title sponsor de la categoría, al menos, hasta 2028. La activación se incluye en el contrato macro firmado por al energética –antigua Cepsa– con LaLiga. Actualmente, la totalidad de marcas que activan con el fútbol femenino de Primera División también lo hacen con el masculino. En este punto cabe recordar una primera decepción para la Liga F en su entrada en la industria del fútbol y no siempre sencillas alianzas comerciales. El primer naming de la categoría lo compró la teleco Finetwork, por entonces muy activa en el patrocinio deportivo. Sin embargo, no llegó a pagar –según denunció después la liga– ni el primer año de contrato. El valor de este acuerdo era de 4 millones anuales. Para 2026-2027, el cambio de ciclo también lleva consigo el fin de la alianza comercial con LaLiga. Se desconoce si la gestora del fútbol profesional español abonará los 10 millones presupuestados para esta temporada, pero ya no actuará como su agencia. Esta pata ya penderá del nuevo brazo comercial que Liga F y Gasol16 Ventures desarrollarán internamente. Antes incluso de la creación de la nueva liga profesional, Mediapro ya apostaba por dar visibilidad al mejor fútbol femenino español en plena guerra por su control entre la RFEF y los clubes. El grupo audiovisual catalán pagaba 2,5 millones de euros anuales a los equipos por los derechos de sus partidos a través de la Asociación de Clubes de Fútbol Femenino (ACFF). Sin embargo, en el verano de 2021, un año antes del nacimiento de la Liga F, la compañía se cansó de la falta de consenso entre clubes –para crear la liga profesional– y de las trabas que se le ponían continuamente para poder revalorizar el producto pese al esfuerzo inversor que hacía en comparación con el retorno real que obtenía. Rescindió el contrato y hubo un apagón audiovisual en el fútbol femenino. Hoy la situación es muy diferente. Se dan todos los partidos en directo y, desde hace unos días, con la garantía de que sea así hasta 2029. DAZN ha renovado como la televisión de la Liga F, lo que le mantendrá como su gran socio audiovisual. La OTT británica ha adquirido el paquete más importante, con el 100% de partidos y preferencia en la elección de los más atractivos de cada jornada. Eso sí, cuatro de ellos los emitirá en coexclusiva con RTVE, que ha comprado el lote dirigido a la televisión en abierto. La ventana de visibilidad que le aportará la cadena pública creen en la gestora que será clave para la revalorización de sus derechos. Además, RTVE ha sublicenciado sus partidos a TV3, por lo que la televisión catalana podrá emitir la gran mayoría de los partidos de sus tres equipos en liza: FC Barcelona, RCD Espanyol y FC Badalona Women. Por ahora no se han hecho públicos el valor conjunto de los derechos para este nuevo ciclo, aunque, según El Confidencial, rondaría los 3,5 millones anuales. Hasta ahora, la liga venía cobrando el doble. Y es que, en su primer acuerdo, DAZN apostó muy fuerte por la competición con la compra de los derechos en exclusiva a nivel global con un compromiso de 35 millones en cinco temporadas. Estos 7 millones anuales se han quedado finalmente en cuatro cursos, ya que liga y OTT acordaron dar por finalizado con un año de anticipación ese contrato que se entiende se firmó con una valoración por encima de mercado para acelerar la profesionalización de la liga. En el nuevo acuerdo se habrían adecuado las cifras a un escenario más realista del negocio actual audiovisual. En el arranque de esta nueva temporada, los principales retos de la Liga F pasan por su autosostenibilidad y un aumento del equilibrio competitivo tras muchos años de férreo dominio del FC Barcelona. Todavía son mayoría los equipos que dan pérdidas y requieren del negocio de su club masculino para poder mantener sus presupuestos. Es cierto que, en general, los ingresos van al alza gracias a los patrocinios, el principal motor de crecimiento del fútbol femenino, pero los números rojos todavía son muy altos: 16,2 millones de euros antes de impuestos se dejaron los equipos en 2024-2025, según datos del CSD. Esto es un 52% más respecto a 2023-2024. Los 16 clubes de la competición asumieron un gasto total de 72,8 millones de euros, frente a los 63,2 millones contabilizados en 2023-2024. El aumento en los salarios de las plantillas tiene la respuesta a la subida. El salario mínimo en la competición se situaba, por convenio, en 23.500 euros en 2025-2026, con opción a llegar a los 28.000 euros si la competición lograba ciertos ingresos adicionales. El coste medio de un equipo que aspire a mantener la categoría es de 2,5 millones de euros, según datos extraídos de Intelligence 2P, la unidad de estrategia e inteligencia de mercado de 2Playbook. Por otro lado, también creció el negocio, pero a un ritmo menor: 56,6 millones facturaron en conjunto, un 8% más interanual. De hecho, sólo cuatro de los 16 equipos lograron beneficios. El Barça sigue como el gran referente de cómo hacer sostenible una estructura profesional de fútbol femenino en España. Por ello, también, llega Gasol16 Ventures, que tendrá el objetivo de que el resto de equipos puedan crecer y generar una independencia del fútbol masculino en todos los aspectos: de estructura, de marca y de negocio. Cuando nadie lo esperaba, el Real Madrid puso negro sobre blanco respecto al acuerdo de 55 millones entre Liga F y el grupo inversor que lidera Pau Gasol. En un comunicado, el club que preside Florentino Pérez detalló que la alianza supone la venta de entre un 35% y un 49% de los ingresos comerciales futuros de la competición a Gasol16 Ventures y Fortified Partners. En concreto, el acuerdo sería por 25 años, hasta 2051. Asimismo, el equipo blanco, contrario al acuerdo, aseguró que los clubes percibirán 40 millones en total, mientras que Liga F recibirá 12 millones. La novedad más relevante es que 3 millones se destinarían a la compra de determinados derechos de imagen de algunas futbolistas. Para el Real Madrid, esta alianza con el vehículo inversor de Gasol “no responde al modelo de crecimiento del fútbol femenino basado en la sostenibilidad, la transparencia y la plena autonomía de los clubes”. Sea como fuere, los clubes favorables al acuerdo son, por ahora, mayoría.

articles.title: Enzo Fernandez transfer news: Chelsea prepared to sell Argentina midfielder to Manchester City for right price
articles.summary: Enzo Fernandez joined Chelsea from Benfica for £107m in 2023; the Argentine played in Chelsea's first Premier League game of the season against Fulham; but was not involved against Luton in Carabao Cup; Chelsea previously set an August 14 deadline for City to bid for Fernandez
articles.body:
There are not believed to have been any club-to-club talks between City and Chelsea yet, but Fernandez was left out of Thursday night's Carabao Cup win over Luton.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso said after the game that Fernandez is a "good professional" who has been training well, and a decision on whether he will be available for Sunday's clash with Brighton will be taken nearer the time.

Man City's interest continues despite missing Chelsea's August 14 deadline to bid for Fernandez.

Chelsea had agreed with Fernandez's representatives that he could be sold for £120m by that deadline but an offer never arrived.

Alonso also said ahead of the Luton game they are "prepared for whatever" happens with any players who could leave before the deadline.

Among the players Chelsea are considering to bring in midfield are Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton. Both clubs consider those players unsellable, however.

City also have Scott as a midfield target as well as Roma's Manu Kone.

Reinforcing central midfield has become an even bigger priority for City following Rodri's departure to Barcelona earlier this month.

Nico Gonzalez has just left to join Newcastle in a transfer worth up to £50m, with Tijjani Reijnders recently departing for Al Qadsiah for £51m. Bernardo Silva also left City following the expiry of his contract and has since joined Real Madrid.

City this week completed the signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille with the midfielder moving to the Etihad Stadium for £86m in a world-record deal for a teenager.

Why Alonso left Fernandez out against Luton

Alonso confirmed in his post-match press conference that he took the decision to leave Fernandez out of the matchday squad for Thursday night's Carabao Cup second-round win over Luton.

"It was just because of the game," Alonso said in his press conference after the win.

"We have other players who need minutes."

Asked when he decided Fernandez would not play against Luton, Alonso replied: "In the afternoon. It's a decision that I took.

"Enzo is a good professional. He's training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight. We will see for Sunday."

Chelsea have agreed a deal worth £7.5m with Aston Villa to sign Emi Martinez.

Sky Sports News reported Chelsea were considering a late move for Martinez after current No 1 Robert Sanchez came under criticism after his error in Monday's win at Fulham.

Martinez has needed to find a new club after Villa signed Zion Suzuki from Parma for nearly £30m.

He was the subject of interest from Juventus but they chose to sign Guglielmo Vicario from Spurs.

Question marks will now be raised over whether both Sanchez and Mike Penders will remain at Stamford Bridge for the season.

Penders started Chelsea's Carabao Cup tie with Luton on Thursday night, after Sanchez started v Fulham.

articles.title: Man Utd have issues defending set-pieces, Ethan Ampadu's long throw a weapon for Leeds - The Radar
articles.summary: The Radar column returns for the new Premier League season with a look at the set-piece issue exposed by Man Utd's opening-day defeat to Hull. Plus, the data showing how Ethan Ampadu has honed his long throw to create a dangerous weapon for Leeds
articles.body:
Welcome to The Radar , a Sky Sports column in which Nick Wright uses a blend of data and opinion to shed light on need-to-know Premier League stories. In the opening edition of the season:

🔺 Man Utd's woes defending corners 🔺 Ampadu's long throws getting longer 🔺 A player to watch this weekend

Michael Carrick bristled at the suggestion that Manchester United's defeat to Hull was down to a lack of passion and made the point that both goals came from set-pieces. It wasn't the first time, though, that defending dead balls has been a problem.

Hull's first goal, a rebound buried at close range by Semi Ajayi, was the 12th Manchester United have conceded from a corner since the start of last season. It is the joint-highest total of any current Premier League side in that timeframe along with Leeds.

Ajayi's opener was of course compounded by Nobel Mendy scoring Hull's second from a free-kick and followed corner goals conceded by Manchester United against Crystal Palace, Aston Villa, Brentford and Nottingham Forest in the final two months of last season.

Unlike against Hull, those goals last season didn't matter. Manchester United ended up winning all four games on the way to their third-placed Premier League finish. But watching the clips back, it is striking just how easy they made it for their opponents.

Like Ajayi, who was able to find space as Harry Maguire inexplicably held his own team-mate Noussair Mazraoui, all three of Maxence Lacroix, Ross Barkley and Morato were unchallenged when scoring their goals for Palace, Aston Villa and Forest respectively.

This frailty when defending corners, and set-pieces generally, was noted by Hull's head coach Sergej Jakirovic, who spoke about making plans to exploit the weakness with the help of his assistant and video analyst in his press conference after the game.

Carrick can, in his defence, point to evidence of overall defensive improvement since his appointment in January. Manchester United had conceded 31 goals in 21 Premier League games before his arrival last season and have only conceded 20 in 18 since.

The fact they have the third-highest percentage of goals conceded from set-pieces in the Premier League since his first game in charge, though, underlines the extent of the issue.

It should be noted that, on the flip side, Manchester United enjoyed considerable success from attacking set-pieces last term. Their total of 26 set-piece goals scored put them second only to champions Arsenal among Premier League sides.

But until they can eliminate their issues in their own box, when the corners and free-kicks are flying in, they risk a repeat of their implosion against Hull. Ipswich, visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, live on Sky Sports , will aim to be the next opponent to profit.

In a summer of high-profile midfield moves by the Premier League's elite clubs, Leeds may feel they pulled off something of a coup by tying Ethan Ampadu to a new contract in June. Their captain, whose deal runs until 2030, continues to excel under Daniel Farke.

Ampadu, rated as an outstanding leader by his manager, and described by Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher as one of his favourite midfielders, offers plenty on and off the ball in the No 6 role, operating as both a deep-lying playmaker and a destroyer.

But his most crucial asset might be his long throw.

His total of 139 long throws into the box since the start of last term puts him behind only Michael Kayode, who he faces live on Sky Sports on Sunday. But he is ahead of the Brentford man for shots from long throws, on 53, and level with him for goals, on five.

Ampadu produced another long throw leading to a goal in Tuesday's Carabao Cup win over Nottingham Forest at the City Ground. It was not his best effort, in truth. The ball followed a looping trajectory towards the near post after slipping out of his hands.

But after Forest failed to clear their lines and the ball ended up being bundled home by James Justin, Ampadu enjoyed turning towards the home fans who had mocked him in celebration.

Ampadu recalls getting stick from his own fans when he began taking them early last season. He said in February: "I got battered a little bit by Leeds fans, saying it wasn't actually that long, which was true, sometimes it's not great. But it's getting longer."

Speaking more recently, after two of Ampadu's throws led to goals against Liverpool in pre-season, his team-mate Brenden Aaronson noted the improvement, describing his long throw as "unbelievable" and adding: "Ethan came back and started throwing it about 20 yards further and 20 yards harder."

Aaronson was of course exaggerating. But the data proves practice is paying off for Ampadu. The graph above shows a steady increase in his average throw distance since February. It now stands at 32 metres, up from around 28m when he started taking them, meaning he is hitting similar distances to fellow specialist Kayode.

Leeds will hope to continue feeling the benefits as one of the defining tactical trends of last season seemingly continues. There were 33 long throws in the opening round of fixtures, roughly in line with last season's record average of 3.9 per game.

Expect a lot more of them at Elland Road on Sunday.

Player Radar: Who else to keep an eye on

Gonzalo Garcia followed up a poacher's finish against Chelsea on his debut with a superb solo goal in Fulham's Carabao Cup win over AFC Wimbledon. The striker, a £34m signing from Real Madrid, will hope to cause problems for Sunderland on Sunday too.

Five Premier League games will be shown live on Sky Sports this weekend, starting with Crystal Palace vs Man City on Friday night.

Saturday's action sees Tottenham host Newcastle , before a packed Sunday schedule. Chelsea take on Brighton and Leeds welcome Brentford in the 2pm games, while Sunderland face Fulham in the other simultaneous kick-off, live on Sky Sports+ .

Man Utd round off Sunday's action against Ipswich at Old Trafford.

There is also a Monday Night Football clash to look forward to, with Aston Villa hosting Arsenal at Villa Park on August 31.

articles.title: El Sevilla ya entrena sin Oso
articles.standfirst: El carrilero fue la única ausencia en una sesión donde Vargas se ejercitó al margen
articles.summary: El carrilero fue la única ausencia en una sesión donde Vargas se ejercitó al margen
articles.body: Este viernes, el Sevilla completó su último entrenamiento antes de medirse al Atlético de Madrid en la tercera jornada de LaLiga. El equipo blanquirrojo se desplazó de nuevo hasta el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán para terminar de afinar la preparación semanal. La única ausencia sobre el césped fue Oso. En estos momentos, el carrilero alicantino viaja a Francia para cerrar su traspaso al Estrasburgo a cambio de 10 millones de euros. “Estoy un poco triste por lo que es el Sevilla para mí, pero ilusionado con este nuevo proyecto”, comentó en el aeropuerto. La sesión matinal también dejó otro nombre propio en el capítulo de posibles salidas. Rubén Vargas, cuyo futuro continúa en el aire, saltó al campo con sus compañeros, pero se ejercitó al margen en la bicicleta estática mientras el club ultima su traspaso. Por su parte, Luis García Plaza, que suele dirigir los entrenamientos a la máxima intensidad, estuvo muy encima de Giorgi Kochorashvili. El centrocampista georgiano ya viajó a San Mamés y podría debutar este fin de semana. Antes de desplazarse al Sánchez-Pizjuán, la jornada arrancó con un bonito homenaje a Antonio Puerta en la Ciudad Deportiva José Ramón Cisneros Palacios. Con motivo del decimonoveno aniversario de su fallecimiento, la primera plantilla se concentró junto a la estatua del canterano para rendirle una ofrenda floral, acompañados del presidente José María del Nido Carrasco. Luis García Plaza comparecerá ante los medios a las 12:00 horas en la sala de prensa del Sánchez-Pizjuán, como parte de la previa de la tercera jornada liguera. El Sevilla recibirá en casa al Atlético de Madrid mañana sábado a las 21:30 horas.

articles.title: Top 7 College Football Head Coaches on the Hot Seat in 2026
articles.summary: Waning job security is never a fun topic, but the reality of being a head coach in college football isn't always pretty.
articles.body:
Waning job security is never a fun topic, but the reality of being a head coach in college football isn't always pretty.

Sure, most of them are highly compensated. Especially within the power conferences, buyouts can range from comfortable to astronomical, too. When a head coach is fired, financial sympathy isn't in rich supply.

But these hot seats, nevertheless, are becoming quite toasty.

As the 2026 season is set to kick off, several FBS head coaches are feeling some significant win-or-else pressure.

Back in 2021, Baylor won a Big 12 championship, beat Ole Miss in the Sugar Bowl and finished with a 12-2 record. It appeared the Bears hit a metaphorical home run by hiring Dave Aranda.

Unfortunately for the school, that's been an untouchable peak.

Baylor has mustered 6-7, 3-9, 8-5 and 5-7 records in the last four seasons, not coincidentally having a single above-.500 Big 12 mark during that run. In short, the Bears have typically been a non-factor lately.

Although the 2026 schedule isn't easy , BU has a favorable path early on. Aranda could have a much safer job by the time November rolls around.

If Baylor is not in a strong position by then, however, a three-game stretch against BYU, Texas Tech and Houston to end the season may seal Aranda's fate.

On paper, it seems like the program is trending in the right direction.

Cincinnati went 3-9 in 2023, the first season of Scott Satterfield's tenure. Since then, the Bearcats have improved to 5-7 and 7-6.

Context, though, is critical. Two years ago, UC ripped off a 5-2 start before falling in five straight games to close the campaign. Last season, the Bearcats put together a 7-1 start but again dropped five in a row.

The issue is not simply that Cincinnati has lost, but also the uncompetitive games. Five of those 10 losses were by at least 17 points.

Considering the second half of UC's 2026 slate includes Texas Tech, Utah, Houston and BYU—all preseason Top 25 teams—Satterfield needs the Bearcats to survive down the stretch. Otherwise, this frustration may boil over.

Following a disastrous 2-10 season in 2024, Florida State opened the 2025 campaign with a shocking upset of Alabama. Not only did the Seminoles win, they completely owned the matchup.

In that moment, the temperature on Mike Norvell's seat cooled significantly. Surely the previous year was just an annoying blip on the radar.

After two painless wins, the 'Noles dropped four consecutive games—with a lifeless loss against a bad Stanford team punctuating an awful stretch. Later setbacks to Clemson, NC State and Florida kept FSU short of bowl eligibility at 5-7.

No matter the timing, Norvell's buyout would be north of $45 million if a change happened this year. That's a real financial obstacle for FSU.

But if the 'Noles struggle again, can they afford to keep Norvell any longer?

Mike Locksley inherited a program in rough shape, and results from the 2020 season can be afforded a little more compassion.

Maryland jumped to 7-6 in 2021, then notched back-to-back 8-5 campaigns. Factor in the realistic expectations at a place not known for football excellence, and that was a major improvement.

That is also why consecutive 4-8 seasons—with 1-8 conference records in both years—aren't sitting well.

Locksley doesn't need to dominate the Big Ten. That's not fair. Maryland, as a university, is not financially able to make a big-money decision of this degree without exhausting every shred of patience, either.

Still, another ugly Big Ten campaign would be tough to stomach.

That's always been the question for North Carolina, which took an extreme gamble when it hired Bill Belichick prior to 2025. He's a football savant, but the NFL legend presumably thought his reputation would be enough to thrive in Chapel Hill. In today's NIL-driven era, that was never likely.

Trotting out a lethargic offense in a 4-8 debut was a problem. North Carolina also enters 2026 amid off-field distractions and questions about the program's direction, including public attention surrounding Belichick's relationship with Jordon Hudson, Michael Lombardi's recent administrative leave and Steve Belichick's medical leave. Whether those factors affect the team on the field remains to be seen.

In theory, Belichick is the smartest guy on the field. In theory, he could elevate a properly built team. In theory, the Tar Heels can ascend.

That vision will become less believable if UNC remains a mess in 2026.

Although on-field results are important, an undeniably massive part of the discussion around Lincoln Riley at USC is money.

While specifics of his buyout are unknown—USC is a private institution—the figure is believed to be around $60 million . If there's any confidence left in Riley by season's end, he'll be back. That number is just enormous.

On the other hand, despite all of the resources provided, the Trojans haven't hit double-digit victories since his debut in 2022.

USC needs immediate dividends from its recent top-ranked recruiting class in order to handle one of the nation's hardest schedules. Otherwise, a new coach may be taking over for Riley next season.

Wisconsin became a highly respected program based on a clear identity. Consistently, the Badgers had a team greater than the sum of its parts, leaning on elite development with lower-rated, in-state talent.

As the sport shifted to its current NIL-driven state, Luke Fickell and UW thought—not without reason—that principle could persist. Fickell also strayed from the proven blueprint as he (understandably) tried to modernize the offense.

During his brief tenure, the Badgers have dipped from 7-6 to 5-7 to 4-8. An impressive 22-year bowl streak ended in 2024, and last season marked the first back-to-back sub-.500 campaigns for Wisconsin since 1991-92.

The bright side is the schedule looks far less daunting overall. But if the Badgers stumble early, a favorable November slate could determine Fickell's future.

articles.title: Stadium closures for Old Firm after fan disorder
articles.summary: Celtic and Rangers are ordered to play their next home Scottish Cup ties behind closed doors after fan disorder last season.
articles.body:
Celtic and Rangers have both been ordered to play their next home Scottish Cup matches behind closed doors after last season's quarter-final was marred by fan disorder.

Both clubs will also have to pay £100,000 to the team they are drawn against in that fixture.

The two clubs could also face a second home match without fans if there is a further incident of either side's supporters engaging in "unacceptable conduct" in a Scottish Cup fixture.

Celtic progressed to last season's semi-finals by beating Rangers on penalties at Ibrox, after which fans of both teams spilled on to the pitch.

The sanctions are likely to come into force when both sides enter this season's Scottish Cup in January.

Meanwhile, Rangers say they will provide Celtic with 300 tickets for next month's Scottish League Cup quarter-final at Ibrox.

Celtic had been given 8,000 tickets for the 8 March Scottish Cup tie.

Celtic 'shocked by disproportionate punishment'

Celtic said: "We are shocked by this disproportionate punishment for a relatively small incursion by Celtic supporters at a moment of emotion and celebration.

"Our club has never defended supporters entering the field of play and we have repeatedly taken action when it occurs.

"However, we understand the part emotion plays in football and would have expected the context and distinction in behaviours to have been taken into account by the panel.

"Another important distinction is that, on this occasion, Celtic were not the home club, responsible for stadium safety arrangements.

"We will study the panel's report and reasoning when it is available and will thereafter consider our next steps."

Rangers said: "We note the decision of the Scottish FA tribunal published today and will now consider the outcome in full, including its implications, before determining any further steps."

Three more arrests after Old Firm fan disorder

Sanctions signal SFA shift in approach - analysis

The sanctions relate to the scenes in March after Celtic's penalty shootout victory, when supporters threw fireworks and other missiles, police officers were injured and a number of arrests were made.

Both clubs gave evidence to an independent judicial panel after being charged under the Scottish FA's disciplinary rule 37, which covers unacceptable conduct at matches.

An independent review published last month concluded the incident came within a "very small margin" of becoming a violent mass confrontation.

The report, led by Mark Blackbourne, identified failings by both clubs and criticised the Scottish FA for not taking a tougher approach to crowd disorder.

In the recent past, the SFA and SPFL have handed down fines and, on occasion, reduced ticket allocations for issues such as the use of pyrotechnics, but the severity of this sanction signals a shift in approach.

The SFA has not escaped its share of the criticism by the independent review, but the panel's report provided the governing body with the cover it needed to get tougher on an ever-growing problem.

And while it comes as no surprise to see the clubs defending their positions, when the dust settles, the SFA will hope that these sanctions will send out a clear message that unacceptable conduct will no longer be tolerated.

articles.title: Xavi Espart: ha nacido otra estrella en el Barça
articles.standfirst: El canterano, de 2007 como Lamine y Cubarsí, tiene asombrados a Flick y a sus compañeros
articles.summary: El canterano, de 2007 como Lamine y Cubarsí, tiene asombrados a Flick y a sus compañeros
articles.body: Xavi Espart ha irrumpido con fuerza en el Barça. En modo arrollador. Contra el Athletic, volvió a salir de titular y estrenó su dorsal número 12, el que acredita y confirma que ha llegado al primer equipo para quedarse. El joven canterano, de 19 años, volvió a dar un recital técnico y táctico, con y sin balón. Tiene asombrados a Hansi Flick y al resto de sus compañeros. La Masía y el Spotify Camp Nou ya tienen una nueva estrella. Otro jugador más, del 2007, que triunfa como culé. Se suma a Lamine, Bernal y Cubarsí. "Aprecio mucho lo que veo de él. Me sorprende que pueda jugar también en la izquierda. Siempre está enfocado, y tácticamente es muy bueno. Estoy muy feliz, es un jugador realmente top. Estoy un poco sorprendido por su temple, por cómo juega... es genial. Creo que no es fácil para un futbolista jugar en esa posición y ha hecho un gran trabajo, con y sin balón. Técnicamente, está a un alto nivel. Espero que siga por este camino, tiene un gran potencial", comentó Hansi Flick tras el partido contra el Athletic. El técnico alemán le hizo debutar el curso pasado, en marzo en la Champions League contra el Newcastle, y fue recurriendo a él. Aunque no tuvo mucho protagonismo, intervino de forma testimonial en seis encuentros, fue entrando en las convocatorias. El preparador no quería perderlo de vista: nada más conocerlo ya le comparó con Philipp Lahm. Palabras mayores que Flick pronunció convencido. Pero el gran salto lo dio esta pretemporada, firmando grandes partidos. "Es un jugador top", dijo el técnico tras varios encuentros de preparación. Tanto le convenció que ha sido titular en los dos encuentros iniciales de LaLiga, contra el Elche y el Athletic. Disputó los 90 minutos en ambos, y eso que jugó en el ala izquierda, a pesar de ser lateral derecho y pivote defensivo. Contra el conjunto vasco, además, Cancelo ya estaba para ser titular, pero el portugués fue suplente. Así mismo, el internacional sub 19 ha adelantado, definitivamente, a Alejandro Balde. El cambio de posición no impidió que Espart desplegara su calidad: inteligencia táctica, sangre fría, colocación, anticipación, buena salida del balón, habilidad en la recuperación... e incluso ¡proyección ofensiva! Contra el Athletic, buscó el gol y obligó a lucirse a Unai Simón en el minuto 59, y dejó también algunos centros magistrales, mostrando su talento como extremo e interior. Combinó bien con Gordon, Raphinha... Además, no se arrugó en cuanto a intensidad, forzando una tarjeta por una falta táctica sobre Iñaki Williams. Su talento ha convencido a Flick. Pero también a sus compañeros. "La defensa, a pesar de que es un sistema que es complicado para esa línea y tiene que estar concentrada todo el partido, ha estado a un gran nivel", comentó Joan García a nivel general para luego concretar: "Xavi Espart es increíble". Pero otro joven de la zaga también se deshizo en elogios hacia el polivalente futbolista, con contrato hasta junio de 2028. "Estamos muy contentos de que esté aquí con nosotros. Hemos crecido juntos en el fútbol formativo, con Bernal y Lamine. Ya lo habéis visto todos: es espectacular con la pelota, puede jugar de lateral y en el medio... y siempre lo hace perfecto", aseveró Pau Cubarsí. Espart suma ocho encuentros en la elite, cinco los ha jugado de lateral derecho, dos de izquierdo y uno de pivote, pero su irrupción no deja lugar a dudas: ha llegado a Primera para quedarse. Lleva la misma trayectoria de sus otros exitosos compañeros del primer equipo nacidos en 2007: Lamine Yamal, Marc Bernal y Pau Cubarsí.

articles.title: Old Firm: Rangers and Celtic both ordered to play next Scottish Cup home game behind closed doors after crowd trouble
articles.summary: The Old Firm clubs were charged following the crowd trouble at their Scottish Cup quarter-final tie in March; the sides meet in the League Cup on September 13; the first Premiership clash of the season is one week later, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The Scottish FA has issued the punishment following the crowd trouble which marred last season's quarter-final at Ibrox.

The two Glasgow teams will also have to pay the visiting side for their next home Scottish Cup fixture £100,000.

A second match stadium closure will be triggered if there is any trouble at a Scottish Cup fixture until the end of the 2027/28 season.

It follows their Scottish Cup match at Ibrox in March when fans clashed on the pitch after a penalty shoot-out win for Celtic.

This was the first Old Firm game at Ibrox since 2018 where Celtic were given the full Broomloan Stand, meaning there were around 7,500 away fans at the game. That figure was agreed to comply with Scottish Cup rules on ticket allocations.

The league match between Rangers and Celtic the previous weekend had around 2,500 away fans after an agreement between clubs to give around five per cent of stadium capacity to away teams for this fixture.

That followed seasons of reduced allocations, or at times no away fans at games.

Celtic progressed to the semi-finals with a 4-2 shoot-out victory over Rangers after the goalless draw at Ibrox, which sparked a pitch invasion from both sets of supporters.

Some visiting fans spilled onto the playing surface to celebrate after the winning spot-kick and supporters from the Rangers end charged towards them with fireworks thrown back and forth.

A total of 43 arrests have now been made in connection.

An independent review into the scenes previously concluded that "crushing" and "life-threatening violence" were narrowly avoided.

The report, led by Mark Blackbourne, found: "The Celtic Ultras were the first to enter the pitch in jubilation, with others following their lead.

"In contrast, the Union Bears' movement onto the track and towards the pitch was reactionary, confrontational, and overtly threatening. In both cases, the proximity of these groups to the playing surface materially increased the likelihood of a mass incursion and contributed to the rapid escalation of disorder.

"The post-match pitch invasion by several hundred Celtic supporters was wholly inexcusable. It provoked an immediate hostile response from sections of the home support, who forced past stewards and police to reach the pitch."

Mr Blackbourne also noted it is "deeply disturbing" that a post-match Glasgow City Council Special SAG meeting recorded that time-served Police Scotland officers were described as "petrified" of policing another match at Ibrox Stadium.

He added: "That word must be read in context, not in isolation, but so qualified, it remains deeply disturbing for Scottish football.

"This reference demands the most serious attention from all parties with responsibility for the governance of safety and security at major football fixtures in Scotland."

Interviewees independently described the organisational characteristics of certain Ultra groups in terms more commonly associated with organised crime groups in the report.

The report called for incidents linked to Ultra groups to come down with heavier sanctions from the clubs.

Celtic say they are "shocked by this disproportionate punishment for a relatively small incursion by Celtic supporters at a moment of emotion and celebration".

They added that "another important distinction is that, on this occasion, Celtic were not the home club, responsible for stadium safety arrangements".

Their statement ends by saying they will "study the panel's report and reasoning when it is available and will thereafter consider our next steps".

"There were wide-ranging accusations about all sorts of misdemeanours. Crowd trouble before, during and after the game. Fans without tickets forcing their way in. Graffiti and damage to the stadium. The list goes on and on.

"Now the punishments have been handed out.

"Last month, there was an independent enquiry about what went on and the ugly scenes and as part of that one of the recommendations was that the Scottish FA were encouraged to look at more immediate and severe punishments. It's safe to say, that's exactly what has happened.

"Scottish football often exists in a blame game about who did what and all the mitigating factors, but both have been handed the same punishment."

articles.title: Ibai Gómez: "Si estoy aquí es porque confío en quedar campeones"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador se estrena este domingo al frente del Real Zaragoza con el único objetivo del ascenso
articles.summary: El entrenador se estrena este domingo al frente del Real Zaragoza con el único objetivo del ascenso
articles.body: El Real Zaragoza debuta este domingo en Primera RFEF con la máxima exigencia de lograr el ascenso. Ibai Gómez es consciente pero no tiene miedo y sí mucha fe en que salga bien todo: "Mi único objetivo es ascender pero está muy lejos aún. Calibrar es difícil pero si estoy aquí es porque confío en quedar campeones. Le doy mucho valor a empezar bien para que la gente se ilusione. Se me ponen los pelos de punta de que si las cosas van bien aquí, esto tiene que ser la hostia". El técnico, que solo tendrá la baja de Diego González, tiene claro lo que espera de su equipo: "Asumimos con naturalidad la exigencia de llevar este escudo aunque sabemos que con la camiseta no se gana. Vais a ver un Real Zaragoza que apriete muy alto, que sea difícil de crearle ocasiones a juego abierto y sea capaz de estar cerca del área rival. He visto muchas cosas del Real Zaragoza de Ibai Gómez en pretemporada pero hace falta sostenerlas en el tiempo". Ibai habló sobre el adiós de Hansson y las llegadas de Iranzo y Ureña: "Le mando mucha fuerza y ánimo a Emil Hansson. Ha sido una noticia dura. Merece todo el respeto y que lo apoyemos. Ureña es una gran opción. Nos puede dar uno contra uno, darnos polivalencia arriba y además es un chaval extraordinario. Le damos mucho valor a lo extradeportivo. Rubo es atlético. Nos da velocidad atrás. Estaba como loco por venir desde el primer día". En cuanto al mercado de fichajes, no piensa que haya grandes movimientos en esta recta final: "Solo espero un lateral derecho y que no haya más salidas. Saidu nos hace mejores". Y es que, el mediocentro tampoco ha entrenado hoy y se habían disparado los rumores de un posible traspaso.
